scope: Design-only NONAUTHOR review of frozen grok-implementation-revision-03: DESIGN, TRIGGER, GROK-WORKER-PROMPT, REVIEW-PROMPTS, SOURCES, CORRECTIONS and ALL-DOCS-READING. The review uses the supplied routing inputs (AGENTS.md, ACTIVE-ROUTING.md, the 2026-09-10 assignment, the develop SKILL.md), the preserved SP05 input, the CLI identity and smoke receipts, control-inspection-01, the revision-02 Opus review, the pinned local-05/12/14/18/22 guides and the original DESIGN items 1–19 as normative. It checks the dispositions of the revision-02 Opus findings, especially the blocking actual-executor/shared-leader gap, and the new qualifications for compatibility/trust, advertised tools, the per-session config overlay, version history, durable task input, voting roles and ADOPTION.json. Excluded: product launch, runtime control verification, product/roadmap/sprint acceptance, and the other fresh revision-03 verdict (not read). Approval covers design scope only. The mandatory pre-dispatch checkout/control tests remain unperformed and are still required before any product Grok dispatch.
summary: Revision 03 closes the blocking revision-02 gap. DESIGN now binds the actual executor rather than the launched client: mode, leader socket or explicit absence, PID, executable/version/hash and cgroup, before and after. It requires tool-child ancestry beneath the supervised pinned executor, or beneath a dedicated leader from the same binary under the same supervision via --leader-socket. Environment controls go in the actual executor's environment with private presence verification, cleanup extends to executor and dedicated-leader descendants, and dispatch fails closed when binding cannot be shown. No new supervisor or framework is added. The sandbox in-process claim matches local-18, including forced in-process execution when a built-in profile fails. The GROK_CONFIG overlay text matches local-05's allowlist and filter-only limits and is correctly marked untested. Source-only/no-shell is the stated default. Voters are named as non-author Opus and Astra. ADOPTION.json is a separate receipt, so frozen files are not mutated. I found no concrete contradiction that blocks design approval. The nonblocking items below mostly concern propagation of the source-only default into the worker template, how to satisfy the tool-inventory gate, and post-run configuration drift.

findings.location: GROK-WORKER-PROMPT.md (startup 'Refresh guarded status/next', 'Allowed local commands ... including startup status/next', 'Run the focused allowed checks', ready-for-independent-review rule) vs DESIGN.md source-only default
findings.evidence: DESIGN makes source-only/no-shell the default absent verified child-environment filtering, with root supplying status/next receipts and running checks. The worker template still unconditionally tells the worker to refresh guarded status/next and run the focused checks. It also allows ready-for-independent-review only after the worker has demonstrated the required local checks. On the default route the worker lacks run_terminal_cmd, so it would report partial/blocked or be pushed toward actions it cannot take. The outcome fails safe but is inconsistent with the default.
findings.repair: Add a short source-only branch. When the shell is not admitted, the worker reads root-supplied authenticated status/next receipts, and root performs the named checks. The worker reports source behavior as traced by inspection and lists root-owned checks as pending. That status counts as ready-for-independent-review once root's checks pass. Drop run_terminal_cmd from the filled --tools in that branch.

findings.evidence: DESIGN requires effective tool identities from 'a verified tool-schema/advertisement source and observed events', says available_commands alone is insufficient, and fails closed otherwise. It never states what evidence would count as sufficient. Pinned local-14 documents streaming-json available_commands with a tools list and a streaming-messages-json init.tools list. Observed tool_call events show only tools actually used, not everything available. The template uses --output-format json, which emits neither advertisement. It is also unclear whether always-on companions count as forbidden background-shell tools. Local-22 lists get_command_or_subagent_output and kill_command_or_subagent as built-in read-only tools. As written, the gate could be unsatisfiable or be read inconsistently.
findings.repair: Name acceptable evidence. Use the advertised tools list from the actual launch or an identically configured harmless preflight on the same executor, plus a denied probe of at least one unadmitted tool class. State explicitly whether shell-output/kill companions are forbidden (remove them) or covered by the descendant-cleanup rule.

findings.location: DESIGN.md sanitized launch receipt and pre-freeze paragraph
findings.evidence: The receipt binds the binary before and after, but configuration, rule, hook, plugin, remembered-grant and sandbox sources only before. Local-18's workspace profile permits writes to ~/.grok/, and local-22 stores remembered grants under ~/.grok/sessions/*/permission.toml. On an admitted shell route, worker-edited test code could therefore persist changes that alter later sessions' effective permissions. Such changes would not show in the owned-path manifest. Control-inspection-01 also shows plugin-provided hooks from unrelated locations (goldbach worktree, superpowers) and home Claude SessionStart hooks.
findings.repair: Re-run sanitized `grok inspect --json` after quiescence, and hash-compare the config, rules, hooks, plugin and grant sources and sandbox.toml before and after. Name plugin-provided hooks/skills among the recorded sources. Treat any unexplained change, or any write outside owned paths in the checkout's git status, as a failed control for that dispatch.

findings.location: DESIGN.md trust sentence; GROK-WORKER-PROMPT.md skill/AGENTS loading
findings.evidence: Pinned local-12 and local-22 say startup loading of project instructions, skills and project permission rules requires folder trust, and control-inspection-01 records projectTrusted=false. DESIGN rightly says to observe trust rather than invent --trust. It does not say that AGENTS.md and skill content reach the worker only through the prompt's explicit read. It also does not say that granting trust would newly load project .claude/.grok rules and hooks, changing the effective permission set.
findings.repair: State that instructions reach the worker through the prompt's explicit reads, not auto-loading. Any trust grant is a recorded configuration change that requires a fresh effective-rule receipt.

findings.evidence: ADOPTION.json must bind the 'accepted revision, manifest hash and both substantive review receipts', and continuations treat mismatch as not adopted. The validated fields are not enumerated. Reviews are issued against both a candidate.json hash and the design manifest hash.
findings.repair: At adoption, record the revision path, the design manifest SHA-256 and candidate.json SHA-256, each review receipt path and SHA-256, the actual returned model/provider, the terminal verdict and the candidate hash each review names. Validate all of these on continuation.

findings.location: AGENTS.md ('Current implementation and review routing', 'Autonomous sprint decisions', final plugin paragraph); SKILL.md Product Routing/review step; assignment file revision pointer
findings.evidence: Loaded startup text still names GPT-6 implementation, Astra/Grok reviews, GPT-6/Grok voters and 'replaces Opus'. The assignment's latest pointer is revision-02. The ACTIVE-ROUTING override and DESIGN's voter naming control, but compaction misreading risk persists (carried from R2-OPUS-9).
findings.repair: After adoption, reconcile these sentences as an ordinary authorized documentation edit. Not required for design approval.

findings.evidence: The table header reads 'Disposition in revision 03' for inherited revision-01 findings. The Opus F1 row cites 'root checkpoint routing fact 374' without the 'unpinned' qualifier that DESIGN applies. Review-01 verdict links are not in the design manifest and are not labeled unpinned. ALL-DOCS-READING (carried unchanged) still refers to the revision-02 correction count.
findings.repair: Fix the wording in any successor. No substantive change.

checks: R2-OPUS-1 (blocking) resolved on current DESIGN text. Executor mode, socket, PID, binary/version/hash and cgroup are recorded before and after. Tool-child ancestry is required, and an unbound shared leader is never adopted. The dedicated leader must come from the same pinned binary under the same supervision. Controls sit in the actual executor environment, cleanup covers executor and dedicated-leader descendants, and dispatch fails closed. TRIGGER now names the 'mandatory DESIGN actual-executor/control gate'. The worker template carries the executor/tool receipt field.

Sandbox claims match local-18 'How It Works': a requested non-off profile runs in-process and refuses the leader even when a built-in profile fails. Setup failure continues unenforced. DESIGN still requires observing mode and enforcement separately.

GROK_CONFIG/GROK_CONFIG_PATH text matches local-05: a deep-merged overlay below requirements, allowlisted to models/features/narrowed toolset/shell_environment_policy filter fields, unable to inject values, with some security gates reading disk layers. The ACP stdio framing is noted. DESIGN marks it untested for headless or leader use and keeps the filtering negative-control gate.

R2-OPUS-2: home and project Claude settings/settings.local, rules/CLAUDE files, Cursor sources, sanitized grok inspect output and observed trust are now named; control-inspection-01 is pinned as discovery only.
R2-OPUS-3: an effective tool inventory is required, with fail-closed on scheduler/monitor/background/unadmitted tools (precision gap noted in R3-OPUS-2).
R2-OPUS-4: source-only is the default absent verified filtering; root runs checks separately.

R2-OPUS-5: 1.0.13 is labeled parent-reported and unpinned. SOURCES notes that revision-01 raw/grok-version.txt reads 1.0.25 and its grok-help.txt is byte-identical to current help. Hashes 97daa4… and 8dd784… agree across manifests.

R2-OPUS-6: the former /tmp task input is preserved as raw/assignments/…preserved-input…md, hash 5049160… in DESIGN, the design manifest and candidate.json. Its content matches the SP05 slice (InvocationID, MainPID=0, Result=success, ExecMainCode=1, ExecMainStatus=0, rejection cases, FINANCIAL_COMPLETE≠exit zero, no dispatch). Fact 374 and the K receipt are labeled unpinned in DESIGN, SOURCES and REVIEW-PROMPTS.

R2-OPUS-7: consequential votes are substantive non-author Opus and Astra votes. Grok proposes but does not vote. Both result audits stay non-author, and original item 11's 'missing providers do not vote' is preserved.
R2-OPUS-8: SOURCES stale phrases corrected. Its closing line now cites both revision-01 reviews and the revision-02 Opus finding, and the table rows are consistent with full reading.
Original DESIGN items 1–19 are declared normative with SHA 3ec27f7c…, matching the pinned original. Only routing and first-task selection change.

ACTIVE-ROUTING, pinned at 579c6c…, requires a sibling ADOPTION.json before adoption and states that adoption never satisfies product-dispatch gates. DESIGN matches, with no circular manifest mutation. Revision-02 artifacts and manifest c4c7ca… remain referenced unchanged.

Design manifest entries compared textually against candidate.json for all 24 listed files plus original design/trigger hashes: all match. I did not compute SHA-256 myself; root verification is relied on.

TRIGGER: 3962 characters with four en dashes (SP01–SP12, MC01–MC08, F0–F3, G01–G24) gives 3970 bytes, consistent with the manifest and under the 4,000-character limit. The trigger carries the no-recreate, no-/loop, no-orchestration, stop-rule, blocked-after-three-turns and full completion predicates.

Permission and headless statements re-checked against local-14 and local-22: dontAsk auto-approvals, remembered grants, Bash prefix/wrapper stripping, conjunctive allow, deny precedence, MCP meta-tools under --tools, fail-open hooks, native json vs streaming-json schemas, and max-turns not bounding tools or spend. DESIGN is faithful.

The review route (claude-opus-5 medium, dontAsk, safe-mode, empty strict MCP, no tools, returned identity verified per review, no approval from exit zero, fragments or timeout) is unchanged and consistent with the revision-02 Opus receipt argv.
limitations: No-tools review. I executed nothing, computed no hashes and read only the supplied packet bytes.

Current 1.0.25 help, parent-earlier help, local-10 hooks, local-17 sessions, local-19 plan mode, local-20 background tasks, local-24 and local-26 were not reproduced. I therefore could not personally confirm that --leader-socket appears in current help, the exact background/scheduler tool IDs, or leader defaults.

The full corpus, both inventories, model-card PDF, revision-01/02 bodies other than those supplied, both review-01 verdicts, the revision-02 Astra review and the root-reported K receipt/fact 374 were not inspected. Historical all-docs reading is recorded, not re-read.

Whether headless 1.0.25 on this WSL2 host uses a shared leader, enforces Landlock/bubblewrap, honors the overlay in headless mode, or has an existing cgroup supervisor are runtime facts outside this review. The design correctly leaves them fail-closed.
ADOPTION.json does not yet exist and was not reviewed.
I did not read the other fresh revision-03 verdict and shared no opinions.

claims: Design approval for revision-03 scope only. No product, roadmap, sprint, proof, Preview, resource or launch-control acceptance is claimed. Product Grok dispatch remains blocked until root records the actual executor binding, sanitized configuration/trust/tool receipts and harmless negative controls for the actual checkout, and ADOPTION.json binds this manifest and both substantive approvals.
